paper.title: Interrogating and Quantifying In Vitro Cancer Drug Pharmacodynamics via Agent-Based and Bayesian Monte Carlo Modelling
paper.displayTitle: Cancer drug pharmacodynamics from MTT data and an agent-based model
paper.authorsShort: Marios Demetriades, Marko Zivanovic, M. Hadjicharalambous, E. Ioannou, B. Ljujic, K. Vucicevic, Z. Ivosevic, A. Dagovic, N. Milivojevic, O. Kokkinos, R. Bauer, V. Vavourakis
paper.affiliation: University of Cyprus · University of Kragujevac · University of Surrey

question: How do eight common cytostatics act on colorectal and breast cancer cells, measured by MTT and reproduced by an agent-based model?

mainFinding.label: as reported
mainFinding.text: Combining in vitro drug screening with an in silico agent-based model reproduces the impact of chemotherapeutic drugs on cancer growth, and characterises each drug through model-derived probabilities of cell apoptosis and division.
emphasis: reproduces the impact of chemotherapeutic drugs
probabilities of cell apoptosis and division

methods.title: MTT cytotoxicity assay
paragraphs: About 10,000 cells per well were seeded in 96-well plates and left 24 h to adhere, then treated with each cytostatic dissolved in DMEM. The concentration range was standardised from 0.1 to 500 µM. Viability was measured 24 and 72 h after treatment.
MTT was reduced to formazan, dissolved in DMSO and read at 550 nm (Rayto 2100C). Viability is the absorbance of treated wells divided by the absorbance of untreated wells, times 100 [ref:20].

methods.title: Statistics and IC50
paragraphs: Six wells per dose. One-way ANOVA in SPSS 17. IC50 values were calculated from the dose curves with CalcuSyn.

methods.title: Agent-based model
paragraphs: Off-lattice, two-dimensional agent-based model of one well (disk, 2.4 mm diameter), built on BioDynaMo [ref:16]. Each cell grows, migrates, divides and can die by apoptosis. Only division and apoptosis respond to the drug; growth (90%) and migration (99%) probabilities are fixed.
The drug concentration is uniform and constant in time.
equations: each step: if r ≤ P_apoptose → remove cell
if r ≤ P_migrate → move · if r ≤ P_grow → grow

methods.title: Parameter estimation
paragraphs: P_apoptose and P_divide were estimated for every treatment scenario with Variational Bayesian Monte Carlo [ref:21], fitting model viability to the MTT viability. Gaussian priors with means 0.2 and 0.15.
notes: Survival probability ratio = (P_divide treated / P_divide control) ÷ (P_apoptose treated / P_apoptose control), §3.3.

limitations.title: Two model parameters are coupled
limitations.text: The authors report that P_apoptose and P_divide trade off against each other, so their ratio is estimated reliably but not each value alone (§3.2, Fig 5).

limitations.title: Two-dimensional, constant drug
limitations.text: The model is 2D and holds drug concentration constant, with no uptake, diffusion or decay (§2.2.1).

limitations.title: Single drugs only
limitations.text: Combinations used in clinical protocols (FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, AC) were not tested here; the authors describe them as ongoing work (§4).

limitations.title: Endpoint assay
limitations.text: MTT reads metabolic activity at 24 and 72 h only. The follow-up paper tracks the same drugs in real time with impedance.

text: Calculation of the IC50 values (Figure 2a) revealed that 5-FU, Ox-Pt, and Irinotecan exerted significant effects 72 h after treatment (IC50 5-FU = 86.9 µM, IC50 Ox-Pt = 89.3 µM, IC50 Irinotecan = 143.9 µM).
In MDA-MB-231 cells treatment, Doxorubicin exerted predominant anticancer activity in both treatment periods.
Comparing the in vitro, blue lines, to the in silico results, red lines, the model demonstrates its capacity to capture the experimentally measured cell viability very well.
In rare cases, the model fails to match exactly the in vitro results, particularly when significant fluctuations are present, as can be seen in Figure 4a.
Although the absolute values of the probabilities cannot be retrieved, their ratio can be reliably estimated.
Values of cancer cell survival below 1 denote a stronger anti-tumoural effect.
